facts.detail: The updated voluntary broadband speeds codes apply to broadband purchases from 21 December 2022.
The current page lists BT, EE, NOW Broadband, PlusNet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Zen Internet as residential signatories.
The current business-code signatories listed are BT, TalkTalk and Virgin Media.
Daisy Communications, including XLN, has not been a business-code signatory since 15 December 2023.

guard_streams.write_limit: Voluntary-code membership is provider-level consumer-protection evidence, not parcel coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: Residential estimated speeds should cover the busy period from 8pm to 10pm.
Business estimated speeds should cover the busy period from noon to 2pm.
A participating provider should provide a personalised minimum guaranteed broadband speed.
For superfast products the minimum guarantee is based on the capability of the line entering the home or office.

guard_streams.write_limit: Sales estimates and guarantees do not constitute independent parcel measurements.

facts.detail: Code signatories commit to provide the estimated speed range in writing at the start of the contract.
Providers should explain technical factors, including distance from the exchange, that may reduce speed.
Providers should maintain robust processes for handling speed-related problems promptly.
Customers may exit without penalty when speeds remain significantly below the original estimate after remediation opportunities.

guard_streams.write_limit: Customer redress is not accepted current postcode-level performance evidence.

facts.detail: Universal service obligations provide a safety net for access to a minimum set of affordable communications services.
BT and KCOM are the designated UK broadband and telephony universal service providers.
Government introduced broadband-USO legislation in March 2018.
Ofcom implemented broadband universal-service conditions for BT and KCOM in March 2020.

guard_streams.write_limit: A statutory request right and designated-provider status do not prove eligibility or current parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage checker guidance and Connected Nations Spring 2026

facts.detail: The broadband USO decent-service threshold is at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload, with additional technical requirements.
Eligible homes and businesses may request a qualifying connection.
The request right remains subject to eligibility and affordability conditions.
Ofcom's checker guidance says premises unable to obtain 10 Mbit/s download may be eligible to request USO service.

guard_streams.write_limit: A checker hint is not a final eligibility decision or exact parcel coverage record.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom upgrading landlines to digital technology

facts.detail: A digital landline normally depends on powered broadband equipment and may stop working during a power cut.
Providers must ensure customers who rely on a landline can contact emergency services during a power cut.
Possible solutions include battery backup or a basic mobile phone.
Telecare, fire-alarm and burglar-alarm equipment using the phone line may require replacement or reconfiguration.

guard_streams.write_limit: Power-cut safeguards and device compatibility are customer-protection evidence, not broadband availability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom protecting customers during digital-landline migration

facts.detail: Providers are expected to minimise disruption during analogue-to-digital landline migration.
Providers must identify, protect and support vulnerable customers during migration.
Ofcom's expectations include at least one hour of power resilience for emergency access.
Published best-practice principles include detailed vulnerable-customer and battery-backup requirements.

guard_streams.write_limit: Migration safeguards do not prove whether a particular parcel has migrated or which access network serves it.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Buckinghamshire Hertfordshire and East Berkshire contract redesign

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 34,000 premises with a £58 million value.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £24.4 million.
The redesign responds to expanded commercial rollout; detailed planning and construction still precede service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned regional scope is planning evidence, not current parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK East and West Sussex contract redesign

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 52,000 premises with a £100 million value.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 13,000 premises backed by £25.2 million.
Commercial rollout overlap, detailed planning and physical network build prevent treating the award as live parcel service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract values and target premises cannot populate exact coverage fields.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 75,500 premises with a £104.2 million value.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 29,000 premises backed by £71.7 million.
The premises list remains subject to detailed-planning and technical changes before service is available.

guard_streams.write_limit: A revised procurement scope does not establish current parcel connection status.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 79,500 premises with a £100.5 million value.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 60,000 premises backed by up to £118.2 million.
The redesign minimises commercial overlap, while detailed plans and technical constraints can still change premise scope.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional redesigned totals are not exact current parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 62,200 premises with a £114.2 million value.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 33,000 premises backed by £61.9 million.
Physical build must occur before service requests, and detailed planning may alter the premise list.

guard_streams.write_limit: Awarded and redesigned scope is not live address-level availability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Leicestershire and Warwickshire contract redesign

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 38,000 premises with a £71 million value.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 36,000 premises backed by up to £76.4 million.
The redesign targets premises otherwise missed by commercial rollout and remains subject to build and technical review.

guard_streams.write_limit: Subsidy targeting and revised scope cannot be promoted to exact parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North Shropshire descoping and reassignment

facts.detail: Freedom Fibre's original North Shropshire award targeted 12,000 premises.
The update reported 2,500 premises built and a further 1,000 targeted by the end of June 2025.
BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually descoped the remaining 8,500 premises.
In April 2026 the affected area was added to Openreach call-off three.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reported build, descoping and reassignment do not identify which individual parcels are ready for service.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Leicestershire and Warwickshire public review readiness definitions

facts.detail: Low-Level Design complete means design and survey work is complete, while build resources may still be unappointed.
Build-team appointed means resources are commissioned and planning, acquisitions and wayleaves are finalised.
In build means construction is underway but premises cannot yet take service.
Ready for Service means build and end-to-end testing are complete and retail providers can offer service to the individual premise.

guard_streams.write_limit: Readiness-stage definitions require premise-specific evidence; labels cannot be inferred from a regional award.
